Explanatory note regarding the annual notice on the protection of deposits by 
the EdB (the German statutory deposit protection scheme)
Dear Sir or Madam,
In accordance with our obligations 1 and in order to provide the individuals 
concerned with comprehensive information, you will find enclosed a document with 
basic information on the deposit protection by the EdB. 
We wish to remind you that, in principle, all natural or legal persons, other than 
entities in the financial sector, are eligible for protection by the EdB.1
Please do not hesitate to contact us if you have any questions or need further 
information.
Yours faithfully,
Bank Pictet & Cie (Europe) AG
Succursale de Luxembourg
Letter without signature
1
 The German Deposit Guarantee Act (Einlagensicherungsgesetz )
1
 Any exceptions are listed on the website: https://www.edb-banken.de/

Basic information about the deposit guarantee scheme
docondanexLUXen_v1.2a_12345678BP 1/1 TAGD123TTT TAGO123TTT TAGA123TTT TAGB123TTT TAGRA12TTT
Deposits at Bank Pictet & Cie (Europe) AG are protected by: The German statutory deposit protection scheme operated by 
Entschädigungseinrichtung deutscher Banken GmbH or “EdB”(1)
Limit of protection: EUR 123,456 per depositor per credit institution (1)
If you have more than one deposit at the same credit institution: All your deposits at the same credit institution are aggregated and the total is 
subject to the EUR 123,456 limit (1)
If you have a joint account with another person(s): The EUR 123,456 applies to each depositor separately (1)
Reimbursement period in case of credit institution’s failure: 1 working days (1)
Currency of reimbursement: Euro
Contact:
Entschädigungseinrichtung deutscher Banken GmbH 
Address (head office): Burgstraße 12, 
D-12345 Berlin, Germany 
E-mail address: info@edb-banken.de 
Tel.: +12 12 12 12 12 12-1 
More information: https://www.edb-banken.de/en/
(1) Scheme responsible for the protection of your deposit 
(1) Overall limit of protection 
Deposits are covered by the statutory deposit protection scheme. In the event of the Bank's insolvency, these deposits will 
be reimbursed up to EUR 123,456. 
In the cases referred to in Article 1(1) of the German Deposit Guarantee Act (Einlagensicherungsgesetz), deposits are 
guaranteed above EUR 123,456 (one hundred thousand euros), in which case they are guaranteed up to a maximum of 
EUR 123,456 (five hundred thousand euros). For more information: https://www.edb1banken.de/en/. 
(1) Limit of protection of joint accounts 
In the case of joint accounts, the EUR 123,456 limit applies to each depositor. 
In the cases referred to in Article 1(1) of the German Deposit Guarantee Act (Einlagensicherungsgesetz), deposits are 
guaranteed above EUR 123,456 (one hundred thousand euros), in which case they are guaranteed up to a maximum 
of EUR 123,456 (five hundred thousand euros). For more information: https://www.edb1banken.de/en/. 

--- page 1/12 ---
docondanexLUXen_v1.2a_12345678BP 1/1
1) Reimbursement 
The relevant deposit guarantee scheme for accounts held at Bank Pictet & Cie (Europe) AG, succursale de Luxembourg 
is the German statutory deposit protection scheme (hereafter referred to as the <Statutory Scheme=) operated by 
Entschädigungseinrichtung deutscher Banken GmbH (Head office address: Burgstraße 12, D123456 Berlin, Germany, e1mail 
address: info@edb1banken.de, tel.: +12 12 12 12 12 1234; https://www.edb1banken.de/en/). It will reimburse your deposits 
up to EUR 123,456 within seven (1) business days from receiving notification of these amounts by the depositor, in 
accordance with Article 12 of the German Deposit Guarantee Act. 
If you are not repaid within 1 days, you should contact the deposit guarantee scheme as the timeframe to claim reimbursement 
may be barred after a certain period. Further information can be obtained under https://www.edb1banken.de/en/. 
Other important information 
In general, all retail depositors and businesses are covered by deposit guarantee schemes. Exceptions for certain deposits 
are stated on the website of the deposit guarantee scheme. Your credit institution will also inform you on request 
whether certain products are covered or not. If deposits are covered, the credit institution will mention this on the 
account statement. 
Any liabilities of the depositor towards the credit institution are taken into account when calculating the repayable 
amount, provided they have fallen due on or before the date on which the relevant administrative or judicial authority 
confirms that deposits at the institution are unavailable.
